body:
closes #21164 as an alternative to #21513 (I prefer Justin's suggested solution)
closes #21513

## Problem

RPC sockets created with `sockconnect()` have no reliable close signal.

## Solution

Add `ChanClosed`, which fires after a channel closes and before the channel is removed.

comment_data.body: Why is `ChanClosed` mentioned here? It's not specific to channels opened by `sockconnect()`.

should we name it `ChanClose` ? to align with `TermClose`, and because `ChanOpen` is not "past tense".

(granted, some legacy event names are inconsistent)

comment_data.body:
nit: seems like the callers of `channel_info_changed` would actually benefit if they just pass the event name.

and this probably means we can just drop `channel_info_changed` entirely :P 


```suggestion
void channel_info_changed(Channel *chan, event_T event)
```

If we could decrement `chan->refcount` *before* calling `channel_event(chan, EVENT_CHANCLOSE)`, that would eliminate the `did_close_event` field.

But I assume we can't do that because there's a potential race? I.e. the channel might get destroyed before the ChanClose handlers execute?
your suspicion is correct, double free found in my experimentation

comment_regular_data.body:
Thanks! Will be nice to finally resolve this. And yes, `ChanClose` parallels nicely with `ChanOpen` , that seems less awkward that doing a callback for "close" and an event for "open".

Not a blocker, but I wonder if we can un-pending the test mentioned in https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/21513 , https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/9456cec7f942c1f98fc3b495a7f90ad603bc631a/test/functional/core/channels_spec.lua#L36
misclick.... implemented the renames though and the un-skipped test passed (no idea how you remember all of these things lol)
